properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by prolonged heavy rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Southeastern Worcester County in central Massachusetts...
Southern Norfolk County in eastern Massachusetts...
Northwestern Bristol County in southeastern Massachusetts...
West Central Plymouth County in southeastern Massachusetts...
Northeastern Providence County in Rhode Island...

* WHEN...Until 145 PM EDT.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring. Streams
continue to rise due to excess runoff from previous rainfall.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 747 AM EDT, Doppler radar indicated continued light to at
times moderate rain falling over the warned area. Between 3 and 6
inches of rain have fallen over the last 48 hours in the warned
area. Additional rainfall expected through this morning could
lead to areas of street and poor drainage flooding. The
Blackstone River above Woonsocket is now in minor flood stage
levels at 11.96 ft, which leads to low- lying flooding along
portions of Cumberland and Woonsocket as well as off of Route 122
in Cumberland.
- Additional rainfall amounts of 0.5 to 1 inch are possible in the
warned area.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Brockton, Pawtucket, Taunton, East Providence, Woonsocket,
Cumberland, Randolph, North Providence, Franklin, North
Attleborough, Norwood, Stoughton, Attleboro, Walpole and
Mansfield.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:

deaths occur in vehicles.

properties.headline: Hydrologic Outlook issued September 27 at 8:56PM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO
properties.description:
ESFGJT

Strong southwesterly winds ahead of a closed low centered over
California will pull tropical moisture from Tropical Storm Odalys and
Hurricane Polo towards eastern Utah and western Colorado, with
atmospheric moisture peaking in our area on Monday. The northerly
extent of the expected excessive rainfall poses a threat to our
southern San Juan river basins. Current forecasts suggest 1 to 4
inches of rain Monday morning through early Wednesday. At face value,
rivers and tributaries will see a rise due to the forecast rainfall.
However, localized heavier amounts could result in flooding across
the southern San Juan foothills and communities further downstream.

Rivers have responded rapidly to recent rainfall due to saturated
soils and increased runoff potential. Thus, prolonged periods of
additional rainfall over these regions would trigger a similar
response. The current precipitation forecast suggests larger peaks in
several creeks and rivers than what has been recently observed.
However, high end probabilistic rainfall amounts (i.e. above 90th
percentile) may lead to rivers exceeding action stage to minor
flooding. Most probable basins to see significant rises include; the
Rio Blanco, San Juan, Piedra, Los Pinos/Vallecito Creek, and the
Animas River Basins.

Convective storms and periods of heavy rainfall fed from said
tropical moisture could result in localized flooding impacts across
the CWA. However, confidence decreases rapidly north of the San
Juans. Confidence has increased enough for a Flood Watch to be issued
for southern portions of the forecast area valid from 6AM Monday
through 6AM Wednesday. Continue to monitor the latest forecasts
especially for those who reside and/or plan to recreate in the Watch
areas.

properties.headline: Hydrologic Outlook issued September 27 at 1:01PM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO
properties.description:
ESFGJT

Strong southwesterly winds ahead of a closed low centered over
California will pull tropical moisture from Tropical Storm Odalys and
Hurricane Polo towards eastern Utah and western Colorado, with
atmospheric moisture peaking in our area on Monday. The northerly
extent of the expected excessive rainfall poses a threat to our
southern San Juan river basins. Current forecasts suggest 1 to 4
inches of rain Monday morning through early Wednesday. At face value,
rivers and tributaries will see a rise due to the forecast rainfall.
However, localized heavier amounts could result in flooding across
the southern San Juan foothills and communities further downstream.

Rivers have responded rapidly to recent rainfall due to saturated
soils and increased runoff potential. Thus, prolonged periods of
additional rainfall over these regions would trigger a similar
response. The current precipitation forecast suggests larger peaks in
several creeks and rivers than what has been recently observed.
However, high end probabilistic rainfall amounts (i.e. above 90th
percentile) may lead to rivers exceeding action stage to minor
flooding. Most probable basins to see significant rises include; the
Rio Blanco, San Juan, Piedra, Los Pinos/Vallecito Creek, and the
Animas River Basins.

Convective storms and periods of heavy rainfall fed from said
tropical moisture could result in localized flooding impacts across
the CWA, however, confidence decreases rapidly north of the San
Juans. Confidence has increased enough for a Flood Watch to be issued
for southern portions of the forecast area valid from 6am Monday
through 6am Wednesday. Continue to monitor the latest forecasts
especially for those who reside and/or plan to recreate in the Watch
areas.

properties.headline: Hydrologic Outlook issued September 25 at 2:21PM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO
properties.description:
ESFGJT

In the wake of today's precipitation, our attention will turn to the
Eastern Pacific. Tropical moisture is anticipated to spread across
the Desert Southwest early next week, drawing moisture from a pair of
Hurricanes; Odalys and Polo. The forecast becomes increasing complex
due to a closed low currently forecast to drive across the Southwest
CONUS as Hurricane Polo approaches the Baja California Peninsula.
Strong southerly winds ahead of the low are expected to pull tropical
moisture towards eastern Utah and western Colorado as early as Monday
morning. The challenge and uncertainty in our precipitation forecast
increase as the week progresses and the low traverses our southern
States. Excessive rainfall is most probable over AZ and NM, attm, but
the northerly extent poses a threat to our southern San Juan river
basins. Current forecasts suggests 1 to 3 inches of rain over Monday
morning through Wednesday. At face value, rivers and tributaries will
see a bump up due to said moisture. However, localized heavier
amounts could result in minor flooding across the southern San Juan
foothills and communities further downstream.

Rivers have responded rapidly to recent rainfall due to saturated
soils and increased runoff potential. Thus, prolonged periods of
additional rainfall over these regions would trigger a similar
response. The current precipitation forecast suggests larger peaks in
several creeks and rivers than what has been observed over the
previous 7 days. However, high end probabilistic rainfall amounts
(i.e. above 90th percentile) may lead to rivers exceeding action
stage to minor flooding. Most probable basins to see significant
rises include; the Rio Blanco, San Juan, Piedra, Los Pinos/Vallecito
Creek, and the Animas River Basins.

Convective storms and periods of heavy rainfall fed from said
tropical moisture could result in localized flooding impacts across
the CWA, however, confidence decreases rapidly north of the San
Juans. Please continue to monitor the forecast as these systems
evolve. Especially for those who reside and/or plan to recreate in
the southwest quadrant of the forecast area.
